observations: Predicate is admitted by the shared Type membership provider only with proven canonical Performances::BooleanEvaluation, Evaluation, Performance, Occurrence and Anything heritage. The library-role witness must be a loaded Predicate, not merely a Function or a user declaration with the same spelling.

Function.result and its checked property now admit Predicate through the existing ordered feature and membership proof. Directed authored Predicate inputs and return Features retain complete owning-signature and positional-redefinition dependencies.

Three new private regressions exercise owned and inherited returns, ordered input replacement, exact parameter/result feature identities, replay without graph growth, public properties, budget retry, missing or wrong-kind libraries, user shadows, missing/cyclic owners and five current-state mutations.

A metadata generation change alone permits a fresh proof. Incomplete metadata blocks both result and feature-domain queries; the test distinguishes these behaviors instead of requiring an error on a valid recertification.

The full 94-file pinned library test checks the Predicate-owned Boolean literal result with both function_result_report and the public Function.result property. Canonical result Type.feature is exactly Base::DataValue::self and Base::things::that.

The expected Boolean result feature was corrected by reviewing Base.kerml: DataValue::self explicitly redefines Anything::self, and Boolean specializes ScalarValue, which specializes DataValue. This differs from the untyped Evaluation.result case retained in the earlier duration test.

LegacyV2 can select the same Predicate return but cannot certify its feature domain without the required Base::dataValues path. Minimal legacy fixtures with explicit required heritage certify the same domains; the checked reader does not invent missing construction.
The selected vendor suite now also runs all 21 existing certified_types module regressions for policy, row-cache invalidation, metadata changes, aliases, relationship carriers and cumulative budgets.
